answer: Sealed Correspondence Ledger. Each identity publishes a fixed pseudonym key and must answer random challenges by signing from the same key within a tight window; a knoll of timed checkpoints records every response. Duplicates reveal themselves because a cloned identity answering two challenges concurrently produces overlapping signatures at a shared checkpoint. Every identity also posts a small atlas of routing paths and a jetty of relay endpoints, so shared infrastructure surfaces across supposedly unrelated identities.
